s15.title: 1690 Orbit | World Champions | Behind the Bumpers | FRC CRESCENDO Robot (auto-caption)

bet.text: Build the shortest, lowest, lightest (to a reasonable extent) and simplest robot possible, with climb and trap only as additions on the main systems.

demand.text: The team decided early not to compromise speaker, amp and fast cycles for anything else. The trap was a "nice to have" on top of existing mechanisms. It set a good-enough shooting distance and focused on making its shots, even if that meant driving a few extra feet.
The main goal was to beat 2910 at its own small, compact style.

auto.text: A seven-piece routine. If the robot reaches the midline and has not picked up a note, it turns, looks for one, leaves the planned path to collect it, then returns to the path, shoots and carries on.
Most championship playoff autos dropped the preload on the way out and skipped the first midline note if missing.

cycle.text: An under-bumper intake takes the note and the trigger rollers feed it at almost any arm angle. The driver drives and presses one button; the robot sets shooter angle, heading and wheel speed. Shots use the estimated pose, so they work without seeing tags.
Against 254 on Einstein it took a longer path to disrupt shots and steal notes.

endgame.text: Light arms open, the hooks pull off magnets as the climb starts, and winches are corrected for roll. One servo releases spring-driven slides and fingers that open the trap door, and the shooter fires in time with the swing.

fallback.text: The championship plan: coming back with under 18 seconds and no amplification in sight, take that note to the trap (under 10 seconds if another note is easy to reach).

gave_up.text: Squeezing the note so the shooter stows between the modules meant spin was not reliable, so the shot has none.
The team warns copiers that other spin shooters, larger intakes, downward amp mechanisms and closer trap mechanisms work better; it perfected only being very low.
A reply from another team counters that its true strength is being fast and controllable.
Good spin would have raised it about 2 in.

changed.text: Both losses before the championship came from a note stuck beneath the shooter; a servo-lifted plate now lets it slide out. Rubber-coated shooter tubes inflated at speed and were replaced by vulcanized rubber. Note-centering wheels came just before the championship.
The trap mostly quit at the championship.
Climb arms were remade for ISR 3, then again after slack rope jammed the winch.

outcome.text: 66-5-1 in official play; won the Daly division, won the championship; captain of the Daly alliance on Einstein; ranked 14 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 54.09, Daly).

facts.text: MA3 absolute encoders, 12-bit PWM; the move from the 10-bit analog version was not really justified
Drive reduction, down from 6.66:1 in 2023
Top speed, measured
The narrow 1 in tread came from a first design around a common 4 in wheel; the team still debates whether it costs traction

functions.name: Low packaging

solves.text: Keep the robot very low without a second mechanism for the amp

functions.type: shooter stows between the swerve modules

facts.text: Whole robot height with the shooter stowed, under
Swerve top plates were changed so the whole shooter fits between the modules
The tube facing the intake (50 x 25 x 3 mm 6061) bent very slightly from impacts and was swapped preventively before the championship; the bend did not affect performance
The main gear plates seemed to take much of the impact; the area was built strong so hits would not move the plates and hurt shooting
Highest point, at the top of the shoulder gear; the rest is around 10 in
Total weight the team gives for the championship; bumpers and battery not mentioned
A steel belly pan keeps the center of gravity low, so fast arm moves caused no noticeable tipping
A very low center of gravity keeps the front wheels loaded while accelerating, and usually wins impacts

solves.text: Take notes without exposing a mechanism outside the bumpers

facts.text: Two powered wheels center the note when it comes in at the side; diameter
Almost nothing leaves the bumpers during a match
Six 1 in silicone-covered rollers run on two Falcons through a 16:24 belt reduction
The bottom roller meets the note first and kicks it up; squeezing notes against the carpet made them stick, pulled a lot of current and sometimes centered badly
A lower top roller needed much more torque with no gain, and peeled damaged notes more
Belts pulling on the middle of the long front roller bent it and skipped, so a steel plate laser-welded to small bearings holds the shafts apart

cost.text: Bumpers mounted slightly lower on the competition robot by accident made the intake worse
The silicone covers on the practice robot got beat up, and alcohol wipes turned out not to be the right way to clean them

functions.name: Trigger

solves.text: Hold a note and feed the shooter at any arm angle without another motor

functions.type: feed rollers shared with the intake motors

facts.text: The arm pivot is concentric with the intake, so a note feeds at almost any angle from travel to amp
Two infrared sensors stop the note
The 20 ms robot loop sometimes missed a sensor reading, so the intake code runs at
Stopping a note: fast to the first sensor, slower to the second, back until the sensor is clear, then forward by
The sensor near the intake mainly catches notes while the wheels are still speeding up, when current draw cannot show one
After the move to 5 ms the note stopped consistently before leaving the shooter
The shooter grabs the note only when the note is tangent to the trigger rollers, because their speeds differ so much

solves.text: One system for speaker, amp and trap that still stows low

facts.text: The note is compressed to about 0.8 of its original width
Two contact points hold the note until the last moment, which gives stability
Rollers are vulcanized rubber fused to aluminum tubes, after rubber coating on aluminum inflated at high speed
Note compression between the rollers, about
Rollers are geared up 60:36 to a maximum of roughly
A higher ratio brought no improvement and a lower one was too slow
The rubber is 3 mm thick on 1.5 in aluminum tube, 44 mm across, and the rollers are epoxied to printed hubs
The note must touch the upper and lower rollers at exactly the same time; touching one first bent it and made shots inconsistent
Two large gears on the motor shafts sync the upper and lower rollers; two motors were kept for quick spin-up in auto
Tests with wheels cut down or removed on one side could not add enough spin to shoot better; notes still tumbled
For the amp the arm flicks and the shot comes mid-flick, because the rollers cannot run at different speeds

cost.text: The compression means spin cannot be added reliably

solves.text: Drive the arm with parts the team can remake and change during the season

facts.text: Steel parts made on the team's own CNC router; the idea came from 971's 2017 turret
Each pinion is two plates with steel pins between them as teeth
The pins are 4 mm steel dowels; a 3 mm end mill on the router cut the rack teeth and pin rings
The rack is leftover SAE1020 steel
A Hall effect sensor checks that the arm starts closed, because there was no space for an absolute encoder on the pivot
Clamp pieces with interlocking edges let the shooter come off the pivot quickly and stay rigid; the main shaft still has to come out too, because a belt ties it to the shooter
For passing, the driver presses a button and the robot picks one of two fixed angles, over the stage or flat, from its position

functions.name: Note deflector

solves.text: Clear a note stuck beneath the shooter, which caused both losses before the championship

functions.type: servo-lifted plate that becomes a slide

facts.text: When the shooter closes, two servos with spoon-like prints catch the plate that protected the power distribution hub and pull it up, so notes slide out
It engages only when needed: the robot rarely needs it, never at the championship, and fewer moving things are more reliable in a small, dense robot

functions.name: Climb

solves.text: Climb with something light and compact added onto the main systems

functions.type: four-bar carbon tube arms with magnet-held hooks and winches

facts.text: Arms of carbon tube and prints open straight up in a four-bar motion
Magnets hold the hooks, which pull off when the climb starts, so the arms only have to open
Winch positions are corrected from the robot's roll
A rope makes a virtual four-bar motion in the arms, replacing separate surgical tubes at shoulder and elbow
The climb line is Dyneema
Single use: the team did not think the slight benefit of several traps was worth the complexity
The winch mounts were made easy to replace, because the team expected to iterate on them a lot

cost.text: One member would change the hooks to be reusable, or build a simpler, harmony-capable climb

functions.name: Trap mechanism

solves.text: Score the trap with the shooter used for everything else

functions.type: spring-driven trap door opener released by one servo

facts.text: One servo releases two linear slides on constant-force springs and torsion-spring fingers that open the trap door; the rest is passive
The same shooter scores the trap, in sync with the robot's swing on the chain

cost.text: The coach says the trap mostly quit at the championship
It worked on about 9 of 10 shots at the district championship, but small differences in the trap door made it inconsistent at the championship

functions.name: Pose tracker

solves.text: Shoot, pick up and drive from a trusted field position instead of the camera image

functions.type: odometry, gyro and tag cameras merged by confidence

facts.text: One Limelight and two other cameras, one for notes and one for tags, the latter two on an Orange Pi with PhotonVision
Each source reports how far off it may be in meters; the positions are merged by that weight
Skids show when the translation parts of the module speeds disagree; the skidding modules are left out of the average
A collision is an accelerometer spike over
After a detected skid the robot will not shoot on its own without seeing a tag
In practice matches it drives the length of the field and multiplies its odometry by the ratio of true to measured distance, because carpets differ; accuracy noticeably improved
Only the angles to a tag come from the cameras; the team's own pose calculation tested more accurate than the Limelight's
The Limelight changes pipelines to see tags at speed and from far away, and runs at about

functions.name: Shooting on the move
functions.type: pose-based shot with robot velocity subtracted

facts.text: Robot velocity is subtracted from the three-dimensional shot vector
Tolerance is checked as meters missed at the target, so it is easier to meet up close
Shots run without seeing tags, which helps against defenders whose flag blocks the low camera

The championship interview says a physics model sets shooter speed and angle; team posts say the angle comes from projectile physics and the speed from a heuristic linear function of distance; the June 2024 slides say note flight was too unstable to model

functions.name: Note detection

solves.text: Recover a missed note in auto and drive to notes without overshoot

functions.type: camera that places notes in field coordinates

facts.text: Distance comes from the note's width, or from pitch when the image edge cuts the note off
The robot drives to the note's field position, which is smoother than closing a loop on the camera
PhotonVision, with the dataset it provides, detects notes on an Orange Pi; the team's code on the roboRIO computes their positions

functions.name: Drive limits and assists
functions.type: physics-limited swerve commands with driver assists

facts.text: Each cycle the driver's command becomes the closest motion the robot can make
A sudden change of direction becomes a smooth arc instead of a skid, with less carpet and tread wear
With the intake button pressed and a note near, the robot adds the motion to take it in the center; the driver can always override
The driver only enables shooting; the robot aims while driving and decides when to shoot
One person drives; another calls out what to look for and can change values such as a constant on shot angle in real time

solves.text: Keep the robot in control, with no skidding wheels and no motors at full power

cost.text: It seems a bit less responsive, which sometimes catches new drivers off guard

decisions.choice: Stow the shooter between the swerve modules
decisions.because: it gives a low center of gravity and one system for speaker, amp and potentially trap
decisions.cost: the note is compressed so far that spin is not reliable

decisions.because: two contact points give a shot without spin more stability
it is made in the team's own workshop, so it can be changed through the season, and a large sector gear sticks out no more than it needs to, while a chain goes all the way around its sprocket

decisions.choice: Build climb and trap on top of the main systems
decisions.because: the team would not compromise speaker, amp and fast cycles, and remembered its 2018 buddy climb

decisions.choice: Do not try to outsmart the game with a complicated design
decisions.because: 2023's robot was super complicated with no real advantage and caused burnout

decisions.choice: Weight each sensor's position by confidence
decisions.because: it is simpler to implement than a Kalman filter and still good enough

decisions.choice: Run the intake code at 5 ms
decisions.because: the 20 ms loop sometimes missed the sensor call that locates the note

decisions.choice: Keep it simple and play with a defender on Einstein
decisions.because: its alliance's offense was notably lower than the others', so out-scoring them made no sense; not passing left no notes to steal, and defense and stealing forced the other alliance to play cycles as well
decisions.instead_of: a passing style, which it had tried mainly as an experiment

decisions.choice: Pick a passing robot second and a defender third
decisions.because: the team knew almost no one else would pick a defense robot, so the best one would still be there

decisions.choice: Finish the design by the end of week 2 and wire the first robot by the end of week 4
decisions.because: shipping and manufacturing are slow, and the software needs time on the robot
decisions.cost: spin was not prototyped nearly enough, and the good-enough bar was set at podium shooting

decisions.because: each robot takes the team a while to make and build, so the practice and competition robots are mostly identical

decisions.choice: Leave amp alignment to the driver
decisions.because: it is pretty easy for the driver
